newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA to resume freight on Nice-LHR route.
newsitem.headline: BA to resume freight on Nice-LHR route.

text.p: British Airways said it will be re-opening its Nice-London Heathrow passenger to freight, effective April 1.

In December 1996, BA decided to close its freight operations on the route because the small volume of shipments it was generating could not justify the deployment of a handling team at Heathrow, a Paris-based BA Cargo official told Reuters.

"The low volumes of freight were largely down to the fact that we were operating Boeing 737 aircraft, which have a very limited cargo capacity and in no way reflected the potential of Nice as a cargo gateway," the official said
From April 1, BA will be phasing out the 737s on the route and instead will deploy two 757s and a 767 to operate the three-times daily frequency.

"While only one of these flights, that operated by the 767, will be carrying freight, it will be able to offer 13 tonnes of palletised space with forwarders also benefitting from an early evening departure from Nice."
The daily 767 flight would give BA more effective coverage of the air cargo market in south-east France, as well as northern Italy, the official added.
BA Cargo had also decided not to renew its cargo sales agreement with Nice-based Southern Airlines Services.

"We will be selling our ex-Nice cargo capacity from the main French cargo office at Paris-Charles de Gaulle airports," the official confirmed. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
